### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f1045bcc7a3e424def90abcc70dc849944b00bd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b271dc9a2afdf17f295c237e5abfa2d13482a5c6` — the merge of head `63f52c544f0ec37a3e16871b069afb762b431cfd` into base `0f1045bcc7a3e424def90abcc70dc849944b00bd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b271dc9a2afdf17f295c237e5abfa2d13482a5c6 && git checkout b271dc9a2afdf17f295c237e5abfa2d13482a5c6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0f1045bcc7a3e424def90abcc70dc849944b00bd 63f52c544f0ec37a3e16871b069afb762b431cfd && git checkout -B drift-repro 0f1045bcc7a3e424def90abcc70dc849944b00bd && git merge --no-ff 63f52c544f0ec37a3e16871b069afb762b431cfd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f1045bcc7a3e424def90abcc70dc849944b00bd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/data/filter-operator-vocabulary.test.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/filter-refusal.ts, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-filter.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts, packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts, ui/packages/core/src/adapters/ValueDataSource.ts, packages/rest/src/data-retired-filter-operator-prescription-door.test.ts (all read in the head tree `prr-27171`, never reviewed)

The rest of the diff (`.changeset/27098-retired-operator-prescription-first.md`, `packages/rest/src/data-retired-filter-operator-prescription-door.test.ts`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` (`session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo`, 09:30Z) and is read here only as cited code.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** The only non-test, non-changeset hunk rewrites two string VALUES (`RETIRED_FILTER_OPERATORS.$regex.why`, `.$options.why`) and adds a docblock paragraph. `RETIRED_FILTER_OPERATORS` is a frozen `Record` of `{ to?, why }`; no key, no `to`, no type changes. Nothing in the tree parses `why`: the six faces that read the table (`sql-driver.ts:2064`, `filter-refusal.ts:735`, `mongodb-filter.ts:1518`, `remote-transport.ts:4505`, `having-filter.ts:394`, `ValueDataSource.ts:919`) interpolate it into a message; `record-validator.ts:556` and `position-catalog-refusal.ts:230` read only `Object.keys(...)`. No filter that was refused is now accepted or vice versa.
- **Public surface: `@objectstack/spec` export VALUE changes, shape does not — right.** `api-surface/data.json` lists `RETIRED_FILTER_OPERATORS (const)` by name only, so the five dist-hash gates stay stable; CI's api-surface / dual-source-exports / entry-nameability runs are green on this head.
- **Wire message for a retired operator changes — right, and as claimed.** Measured on the head strings (string arithmetic on `git show prr-27171:packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`, no build): in the new `$regex` `why`, `` `$icontains` `` sits at offset 4, `` `$contains` `` at 99, "match in application code" ends at 276 and the prescription sentence ends at 277; the history ("`$regex` was never declared …") begins at 389. After `SqlDriver`'s lead-in for field `title` (124 chars) the prescription ends at wire offset 401; after `having`'s (104 chars) at 381 — the dev's two numbers reproduce exactly. In the `$options` `why`, "Delete `$options`" opens the string and `` `$icontains` `` sits at 29. On `main` (merge-base `1900c02c`) the same operator was first named at 566 — past the 500 cap even before any lead-in.
- **Every operator the new prescriptions name exists and is described truthfully — right.** `$icontains` and `$contains` are both keys of `StringOperatorSchema` and members of `FILTER_OPERATORS`. "`$contains` for a case-sensitive one" matches `CONTAINS_DESCRIPTION` ("CASE-SENSITIVELY … case-exact on every JS evaluation face … Lowered to LIKE (case-exact) on the SQL family"). "`$icontains` folds ASCII case" matches `ICONTAINS_DESCRIPTION` ("ONLY ASCII case"). "Both match the comparand literally, so "." and "%" are ordinary characters" matches `LITERAL_COMPARAND_DESCRIPTION`, which both operators carry. "a pattern that genuinely needs a regex has no filter-level replacement" agrees with `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx:369-371` and semantic migration entry 17. The history clauses (LIKE-escaped on driver-sql, real `RegExp` on driver-memory, no `REGEXP` over turso's wire) are carried over from the old text verbatim.
- **Cap, truncation, envelope untouched — right.** `packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts:46,84-86` is not in the diff; `CLIENT_MESSAGE_MAX = 500` and `slice(0, 499) + '…'` stand. The ruling's ⛔ (cap stays, ADR-0112 envelope stays) is honoured.
- **Stale restatements: none.** `git grep` on the head for the old `$regex`/`$options` phrasings ("Its only real use was", "Write `$icontains` for the", "was never a predicate", "regex-flags companion") finds only the new strings themselves, one UI test TITLE, and CHANGELOG history. `scripts/check-corpus-claim-drift.mjs:283-287` and `query-syntax.mdx:355-371` restate the prescription in their own words and are unaffected. The only test touching the surviving history phrase (`memory-analytics-filter-refusal.test.ts:204`) deliberately does NOT assert on it.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27098-retired-operator-prescription-first.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, both declarations line-initial in the changeset and the PR body. **Correct.** Under AGENTS.md §3 the level follows the kind: `Metadata-protocol: none` (a refusal's wording is not a change to what an author can write) takes `patch`; a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`, never `skip-changeset`. `@objectstack/rest` receives a new test file only and publishes nothing, so no second changeset is owed.
- **`Clause-②: no` holds**, with no arm. The spec's own claim in the changeset body ("the table, the operators it names, the cap and the error envelope are unchanged; only the order and wording of the two `why` strings change") is true of the tree, not just the body: ① above traces every reader of the table and none decides acceptance on `why`.
- The changeset carries no ADR-0087 disposition comment, and needs none: nothing is removed, renamed or tombstoned.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `deviations` (os-dev-report `6465060637`):
1. "Clause-② declared plain `no`" against the claim's pre-written "`no` (likely)" — **answered: right**, see ②.
2. The door test marks the caller's `where` as `'author'` through a middleware copying `SecurityPlugin`'s identity check (`where === opCtx.options?.where`) — **answered: a sound rig.** `sql-driver.ts`'s `retiredFilterOperatorError` hands `full` to `withheldFilterError`, which prints the words only for a positively `'author'`-marked subtree (the #8220 contract); without the mark the rig would assert on the withheld class sentence and prove nothing about the prescription. This is a `packages/rest` file and belongs to the lane seat's ACCEPT; read here, not reviewed.
3. Lint run as `eslint --no-inline-config` over the two touched packages, not repo-wide — **answered: covered**, the repo lint check-run on the head is green.

`open_questions`: `[]` — nothing to answer.

`out_of_scope_findings` disposition: the 500-cap census was filed by the seat as #27173 (temporal-comparand and text-operator-declared-type doors); the `$null` sentence is pinned truncated on purpose and left unfiled — agreed. The `{ $regex, $options }` sibling sentence ("one `$icontains` replaces the whole shape") is appended AFTER `why` by every builder and is therefore still cut for the pair after this change — **escalated as a should-fix follow-up, not a defect of this PR**: it lives in the five builders, outside the `hits` file, and the card's Expected ("the refusal names the replacement operator in full") is met for both operators singly; an author who swaps `$regex` for `$icontains` and leaves `$options: 'i'` gets one extra round-trip whose message opens with "Delete `$options`". Named here so the follow-up has a carrier.

Process flag, escalated for the maintainer's attention, not a tree finding: PR #27171 was merged by `objectstack-fleet[bot]` at 2026-10-28T09:53:31Z (merge commit `e5b5c5b0`), three seconds after the triage seat's Contract-review-claim comment (09:53:28Z) and before any `## Contract review` record existed on the head. The seat's ACCEPT notes `check-governed-merges --pr 27171` read NOT governed, while this brief's `reviewFace` puts `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts` on the schema face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Whichever recogniser is right about the landing rule, this record is rendered post-merge and governs the head either way; the two recognisers disagreeing on a `packages/spec` path is the thing to look at.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts` — judged against the ruling it implements (triage `6461925519`: "put the prescription first, keep it outside the cap, or lift the cap … ⛔ the cap stays"), the seat's pick (prescription first at the producer, no cap change), the first consumers (the six faces above and the 500-char client cut), and the scenario it is accepted against (`POST /api/v1/data/OBJECT/query` with `{ title: { $regex: 'acme' } }`, QA run #26476).

**Holds. No must-fix.**

- *Prescription-first is the right lever and is applied at the one source.* The ruling offered three routes; the chosen one changes no code path, no cap and no envelope, and reaches all six faces at once because each prints `why` verbatim. The two routes not taken (a per-code cap exception, a second channel outside the cap) would each have put a special case into `packages/types` for one producer; the pick is the smaller change and the claim's ⛔ lines are respected.
- *Does the budget survive long names?* Tried to break it: with a 60-character field name, a 40-character path and (turso remote) a 40-character object name, the longest lead-in (`[RemoteTransport] … on 'OBJECT.FIELD' …`) is 231 chars; `` `$contains` `` then lands at wire offset 341 and "match in application code" at 507 — the second clarifying sentence is cut, every operator name and the "no filter-level replacement" clause survive. With realistic names (the dev's `title`) the whole prescription including the literal-comparand note ends at 401–417 on every face. The design degrades in the right order: operators first, qualifiers second, history last.
- *The spec pin (`filter-operator-vocabulary.test.ts`, new case) is a sound guard, not a transcription pin.* It asserts a PROPERTY of every entry — at least one declared operator is named in backticks, and each declared operator named first appears before offset 300 — rather than the string's text. It filters through `declaredKeys()` (`FieldOperatorsSchema.shape`), so `$regex`/`$options` in backticks do not count and a prescription naming an undeclared operator still fails the neighbouring "never points at an operator the protocol no longer has" case. It is red on the `main` text (566) and green here (99), so it detects exactly the regression this card is about: history re-ordered in front of the alternatives. Budget 300 = 500 − 200, which the lead-in arithmetic above supports (longest bare lead-in 131 chars, leaving about 70 for names). Two limits, neither a defect: (a) it measures `why` alone, not the wire, so a builder that grows its own lead-in is not caught here — the REST door test is the wire pin for `where` and `having`, which is the right split (spec pins the spec, rest pins the door); (b) it recognises operators only in backticks, which is the convention both entries use and the "states the replacement inside the prescription" case already relies on.
- *Nothing the new text says is wrong about the declared operators* (traced in ①), and nothing it dropped was load-bearing: the old `why`'s "ASCII case fold; the comparand is matched literally, so "." and "%" are ordinary characters" is kept as the second sentence; the old `$options` text's "folds ASCII case on every backend" is kept.
- *First consumer at the door:* the REST test's `mustRead` substrings (`"$regex"`, `$icontains`, `` `$contains` for a case-sensitive one ``, `match in application code`; `"$options"`, `` Delete `$options` ``, `$icontains`) each occur in the head strings at the offsets above and inside 500 after the measured lead-ins; CI confirms (rest and spec suites green on the head).

**should-fix** (non-blocking, both outside the `hits` hunks' own behaviour):
1. The new docblock on `RetiredFilterOperatorGuidance.why` says "each site prints this string after a lead-in of its own naming the operator, the field and {@link to}". The UI face (`ValueDataSource.ts:921-923`) prints `filter operator '…' on field '…' is retired. ${why}` and does not name `to`; and the same docblock's older sentence still counts "five refusal sites" where the tree has six readers. Harmless today because the new `why` names `$icontains` at offset 4, so that face's reader gets it anyway. A one-line precision fix next time the file is touched.
2. The sibling sentence for the `{ $regex, $options }` pair (see ③) — a follow-up card against the five builders, moving the "one `$icontains` replaces the whole shape" clause before `why`, or folding it into the lead-in.
